ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, point $P$ is a moving point on the hypotenuse $AC$ (not coinciding with $A$ or $C$) of $\triangle ABC$. Draw $PM\perp AB$ intersecting $AB$ at point $M$, and draw $PN\perp BC$ intersecting $BC$ at point $N$. Connect $MN$. If $AB=6$ and $BC=8$, then what is the minimum value of $MN$ when point $P$ moves along $AC$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Draw a line PB, \\
$\because$ $\angle ABC=90^\circ$, AB = 6, BC = 8, \\
$\therefore$ $AC=\sqrt{AB^2+BC^2}=\sqrt{6^2+8^2}=10$, \\
$\because$ PM $\perp$ AB, PN $\perp$ BC, $\angle C=90^\circ$, \\
$\therefore$ $\angle PMB=\angle PNB=\angle B=90^\circ$, \\
$\therefore$ Quadrilateral BNPM is a rectangle, \\
$\therefore$ MN = BP, \\
$\because$ The perpendicular segment is the shortest, \\
$\therefore$ When BP $\perp$ AC, the length of MN is minimized, \\
$\therefore$ ${S}_{\triangle ABC}=\frac{1}{2}BC\cdot AB=\frac{1}{2}AC\cdot BP$, \\
$\therefore$ $\frac{1}{2}\times 8\times 6=\frac{1}{2}\times 10\cdot BP$, \\
Solve for it: BP = 4.8. \\
$\therefore$ The minimum value of MN is $\boxed{4.8}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the attached figure, triangle ABC is a right triangle, A is at the upper left, B is at the lower left, C is at the lower right, AB is vertical, and BC is horizontal, so the right angle is at B; P is located on the hypotenuse AC; from P, draw a perpendicular to AB reaching M, and in the figure PM is horizontal; from P, draw a perpendicular to BC reaching N, and in the figure PN is vertical; after connecting MN, BNPM forms a rectangle, and MN is one diagonal of this rectangle. Reasoning: additionally connect BP, then BP is the other diagonal of rectangle BNPM. The two diagonals of a rectangle are equal, so MN = BP. Thus finding the minimum value of MN is equivalent to finding the minimum value of BP when P moves on AC. The distance from a point to a line is shortest, so when BP is perpendicular to AC, BP is minimum. It is known that AB = 6, BC = 8, and ∠B = 90°, so AC = sqrt(6^2 + 8^2) = 10. Use area to calculate the height from B to AC: S△ABC = (1/2)·AB·BC = (1/2)·6·8 = 24, and at the same time S△ABC = (1/2)·AC·BP_min = (1/2)·10·BP_min. Therefore 24 = 5·BP_min, obtaining BP_min = 24/5 = 4.8. Because MN = BP, the minimum value of MN is 4.8.
